subject.title: fix(gateway): skip Control UI pairing for trusted-proxy authenticated operators [AI-assisted]

question: Should successful trusted-proxy authentication be allowed to replace Control UI device pairing for operator WebSocket sessions?
rationale: The PR is technically narrow, but it decides whether reverse-proxy identity becomes the privileged operator boundary for Control UI access, reversing a prior security-hardening PR while matching current docs.

options.title: Approve no-pairing trusted-proxy operators
options.body: Accept reverse-proxy identity as the Control UI operator boundary for trusted-proxy mode and land the narrow runtime/test change after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Keep paired-device baseline
options.body: Reject or pause this PR and update trusted-proxy docs/tests so operators know scoped Control UI access still requires device pairing.

options.title: Split into explicit opt-in policy
options.body: Add a named opt-in policy with tests for the default pairing-required path and the relaxed trusted-proxy path before merge.

recommendation.title: Approve no-pairing trusted-proxy operators
recommendation.body: Accept reverse-proxy identity as the Control UI operator boundary for trusted-proxy mode and land the narrow runtime/test change after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the earlier trusted-proxy skip-pairing behavior and posted the landing proof, making him the clearest available routing owner for this contract choice.
